questions.q: Sanskrit belongs to which language family?
questions.exp: Sanskrit belongs to the Indo-European language family, specifically the Indo-Iranian branch. It is one of the oldest Indo-European languages and the liturgical language of Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.

questions.q: The oldest text written in Sanskrit is?
questions.exp: The Rig Veda is the oldest text written in Sanskrit, dating back to approximately 1500–1200 BCE. It contains 1028 hymns dedicated to various deities.

questions.q: 'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from which Sanskrit text?
questions.exp: 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth alone triumphs) is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad. It is the national motto of India and is inscribed on the national emblem.

questions.q: Who is considered the greatest Sanskrit grammarian?
questions.exp: Panini (c. 4th century BCE) is considered the greatest Sanskrit grammarian. His work Ashtadhyayi contains 3,959 rules of Sanskrit morphology, syntax, and semantics.

questions.q: The Bhagavad Gita is part of which epic?
questions.exp: The Bhagavad Gita is part of the Mahabharata, specifically the Bhishma Parva (chapters 23–40). It contains the conversation between Prince Arjuna and Lord Krishna before the Kurukshetra War.

questions.q: What does the Sanskrit word 'Yoga' mean?
questions.exp: The Sanskrit word 'Yoga' means 'union' or 'to yoke'. It refers to the union of individual consciousness with universal consciousness. It encompasses physical, mental, and spiritual practices.
Kalidasa is considered the greatest poet and playwright in Sanskrit literature. His famous works include Meghaduta (cloud messenger), Shakuntala (a play), and Raghuvamsha (an epic poem).

opts: I bow to the divine in you
questions.exp: 'Namaste' is derived from Sanskrit: 'Namas' (bow, obeisance) + 'Te' (to you). It means 'I bow to the divine in you' or 'The divine in me recognizes the divine in you'.

questions.q: How many letters are in the Sanskrit alphabet?
questions.exp: The Sanskrit alphabet (Devanagari) has 48 letters (some sources say 46 or 52). It consists of 13 vowels and 35 consonants, arranged scientifically according to phonetics.
The word 'Veda' comes from the Sanskrit root 'vid' meaning 'to know'. Thus, Veda means 'knowledge' or 'wisdom'. The four Vedas (Rig, Sama, Yajur, Atharva) are considered revealed scriptures.
